clue.text: Uniform firms' chartered organisations

parts.note: livery is a distinctive uniform worn by servants or staff
firms are companies

explanation.surface: Businesses that share a uniform are being described as official chartered bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The livery companies are the ancient trade guilds of the City of London, many granted royal charters.
explanation.definitionFit: London's livery companies are historic trade guilds, each incorporated by royal charter, so they are chartered bodies.

clue.text: Small telescope for agent's lightweight girl

parts.note: an agent is a spy
G, a gram, is a light unit of weight
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A spy's slim girlfriend is apparently the reason for a little telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' looks like a description of the girl, but it is a separate piece: a gram is a very light weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope of the kind sailors used.

clue.text: Pale, like chicken

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone has gone as white as a frightened chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey-white like ash, a synonym for pale in the face.

clue.text: Old boy embroiled in fiscal trouble producing glasses

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil caught up in a financial scandal ends up needing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: The old boy's two letters join the word fiscal, and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocals are spectacles with lenses split into two zones for near and far vision.

clue.text: Bed aboard, a big one for top gun

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sleeping place on a ship is somehow linked with a top-ranking gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha was the nickname of a huge German howitzer of the First World War, so a big one of the name is a top gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase points to the gun nicknamed Big Bertha, a giant siege howitzer, by its given name.

clue.text: About Archer's place in university

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
Ambridge is the fictional village where the Archers family live in the BBC radio soap The Archers

explanation.surface: An archer's position in some university club is being placed approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera set in the village of Ambridge; 'Archer' is a member of that family, not a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is the English city famous for its ancient university, used here as the name of that university.

clue.text: Enemy I converted was born in Aden

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A one-time enemy, having changed religion, turns out to have been born in Aden.
explanation.walkthrough: Aden is a port city in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is in Yemen, so someone native to it is Yemeni by nationality.

clue.text: Novel, one to read at home with Miss O'Hara, say

parts.note: a means one
to read a subject at university is to study it
someone at home is in

indicators.note: say asks for the name as spoken, so its spelling may differ from what is written

parts.note: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind; the colour word sounds the same with one T

explanation.surface: Someone stays home to read a novel featuring Scarlett O'Hara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the last piece on; Miss O'Hara's first name has a double T, so only its sound is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A Study in Scarlet is the 1887 Arthur Conan Doyle novel that introduced Sherlock Holmes.

clue.text: On the motorway, turning back, a voice becomes unresponsive

indicators.note: turning back means heading the opposite way, so the motorway's name is read right to left

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 written as the letter I
the passive is a grammatical voice, as opposed to the active

explanation.surface: A driver doing a U-turn on the motorway finds a voice going quiet and unresponsive.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its digit as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion or reaction, a synonym for unresponsive.

clue.text: Beats criminal and gives assistance to another?

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thug beats someone and then helps an accomplice, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that abetting usually means helping a wrongdoer, which ties to 'criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone else, typically in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Cretan artist's Spanish style

parts.note: surface reading: the manner in which a painter from Crete painted while in Spain
setter's reading: the style of name, here the Spanish nickname, by which the Cretan painter is known

explanation.surface: An art critic describes how a painter from Crete adopted a Spanish manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Doménikos Theotokópoulos was born on Crete and worked in Toledo, where he was known by a Spanish nickname meaning 'the Greek'.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter is universally known by his Spanish nickname, a title in the Spanish style rather than his Greek birth name.

clue.text: Dramatic spectacle of gold on board

indicators.note: in an across answer, placed on means coming after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A treasure display with gold laid out on a board makes quite a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, especially a group of motionless figures arranged on stage.

clue.text: Agreement the Queen followed for a time

indicators.note: one thing followed by another puts the second after the first in the answer

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, a vote of agreement
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch's agreement came after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time of twelve months.

clue.text: Mr Brown's potential

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nickname of Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener

explanation.surface: Someone is assessing what Mr Brown might achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot Brown got his nickname from telling clients their grounds had great possibilities; 'Mr Brown's' is read as 'Mr Brown is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardener was known by this word as his first name, and the word itself means ability not yet realised.

clue.text: Vetoes films that are not positive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: refusals, a no vote
second meaning: developed photographic film with light and dark reversed
third meaning: things that are the opposite of positive

explanation.surface: A censor rejects any film that is not upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings rather than two: refusals, photographic film strips, and things that are not positive.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers refusals, reversed photographic images and statements of the opposite of positive.

clue.text: Seafood's unusual story absorbs egghead at one point

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into the other
something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
read as the head of egg, its first letter
S, south, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: An odd tale about a brainy person and seafood at one stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a clever person, but it is just the first letter of egg; 'Seafood's' is read as 'Seafood is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are shellfish eaten as a delicacy, a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Old English dialect spoken by Anglican, not Catholic

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation that follows is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: An old dialect is said to be spoken by Anglicans but not Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious surface misleads: the clue simply drops one letter from the church word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian was one of the main dialects of Old English, spoken by the Angles in eastern England.

clue.text: Hand over sailor to police officer before a large number had dinner

indicators.note: one thing before another puts the first earlier in the answer

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
DI is a detective inspector
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to have dinner is to eat, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A sailor is handed to a policeman before a crowd sits down to dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or responsibility, handing it over to someone else.

clue.text: It's understood that naughty child's legitimate

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
licit means lawful, legitimate

explanation.surface: It is accepted that a badly behaved child is a lawful heir after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied without being stated, so it is tacitly understood.

clue.text: US zone improvement plan's correspondent in Britain

definitions.text: US zone improvement plan's correspondent in Britain

parts.words: US zone improvement plan's correspondent in Britain
parts.note: surface reading: a British journalist reporting on an American regional development scheme
setter's reading: ZIP, as in ZIP code, whose British counterpart is the mail-sorting code

explanation.surface: A British reporter covering an American regeneration programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The American ZIP code stands for Zone Improvement Plan; 'correspondent' means equivalent, not a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The British equivalent of an American ZIP code is the alphanumeric postal code used to sort mail.

clue.text: Bird's skin is broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird has broken skin after an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Charlie can go up for a drink

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, the opposite way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is allowed to go up to the bar for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Each part is carved — initially it's impressive

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A sculptor's work is impressive because every part has been carved.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic, used informally, means grand or heroic in scale, so impressive.

clue.text: Issue causing worry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offspring, a family of young
second meaning: to dwell anxiously on something

explanation.surface: A problem that keeps someone anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means a problem in the surface, but here it means children, as in legal language.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is an old legal word for offspring, a brood; to brood is to fret over something.

clue.text: Getting cosy in the Northeast's smart

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for northeast
smart as a verb means to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Settling in comfortably in the stylish northeast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the adjective for stylish, but it is the verb for a sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting means settling into a snug home, an idiom for getting comfortable and domestic.

clue.text: Bag a transmitter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Britain, a plastic or paper shopping bag with handles
second meaning: something that passes on a disease or signal

explanation.surface: An order to grab a radio transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' reads as a verb meaning grab, but it is the noun, as in a British carrier bag for shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier is a shopping bag in British usage, and also anyone who passes on an infection or a radio signal.

clue.text: Expat abstainers run out of textile

indicators.note: to be run out of a place is to be driven away from it, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes people who abstain from alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: Non-drinking expatriates are driven out of the cloth trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for teetotallers are removed from the cloth word, one from each place they occur.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone living away from their homeland, like an expatriate, though usually not by choice.

clue.text: Writer is English, that's clear

parts.note: an author is a writer
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A writer is English, and that is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective meaning obvious, but it is the verb for giving approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something, as in clearing a plan, is to give official permission, which is to authorise it.
